facts.fact: A volume boot record ( VBR ) is a type of boot sector introduced by the IBM Personal Computer.
facts.supporting_span: A volume boot record ( VBR ) ( also known as a volume boot sector , a partition boot record or a partition boot sector ) is a type of boot sector introduced by the IBM Personal Computer .

facts.fact: A volume boot record ( VBR ) is also known as a volume boot sector.
facts.supporting_span: A volume boot record ( VBR ) ( also known as a volume boot sector , a partition boot record or a partition boot sector )

facts.fact: A volume boot record ( VBR ) may be found on a partitioned data storage device or an unpartitioned device.
facts.supporting_span: It may be found on a partitioned data storage device , such as a hard disk , or an unpartitioned device , such as a floppy disk , and contains machine code for bootstrapping programs ( usually , but not necessarily , operating systems ) stored in other parts of the device .

facts.fact: A volume boot record ( VBR ) contains machine code for bootstrapping programs stored in other parts of the device.
facts.supporting_span: and contains machine code for bootstrapping programs ( usually , but not necessarily , operating systems ) stored in other parts of the device .

facts.fact: On non-partitioned storage devices, a volume boot record ( VBR ) is the first sector of the device.
facts.supporting_span: On non - partitioned storage devices , it is the first sector of the device .

facts.fact: On partitioned devices, a volume boot record ( VBR ) is the first sector of an individual partition on the device.
facts.supporting_span: On partitioned devices , it is the first sector of an individual partition on the device , with the first sector of the entire device being a Master Boot Record ( MBR ) containing the partition table .

facts.fact: The first sector of the entire device is a Master Boot Record ( MBR ) containing the partition table.
facts.supporting_span: with the first sector of the entire device being a Master Boot Record ( MBR ) containing the partition table .

facts.fact: The code in volume boot records is invoked either directly by the machine's firmware or indirectly by code in the master boot record or a boot manager.
facts.supporting_span: The code in volume boot records is invoked either directly by the machine 's firmware or indirectly by code in the master boot record or a boot manager .

facts.fact: Invoking a VBR via a boot manager is known as chain loading.
facts.supporting_span: Invoking a VBR via a boot manager is known as chain loading .

facts.fact: Some dual-boot systems, such as NTLDR, take copies of the bootstrap code that individual operating systems install into a single partition's VBR.
facts.supporting_span: Some dual - boot systems , such as NTLDR ( the boot loader for all releases of Microsoft 's Windows NT - derived operating systems up to and including Windows XP and Windows Server 2003 ) , take copies of the bootstrap code that individual operating systems install into a single partition 's VBR

facts.fact: Some dual-boot systems, such as NTLDR, load the relevant VBR content from file after the boot loader has asked the user which operating system to bootstrap.
facts.supporting_span: Some dual - boot systems , such as NTLDR ( the boot loader for all releases of Microsoft 's Windows NT - derived operating systems up to and including Windows XP and Windows Server 2003 ) , take copies of the bootstrap code that individual operating systems install into a single partition 's VBR and store them in disc files , loading the relevant VBR content from file after the boot loader has asked the user which operating system to bootstrap .

facts.fact: NTLDR is the boot loader for all releases of Microsoft's Windows NT-derived operating systems up to and including Windows XP and Windows Server 2003.
facts.supporting_span: NTLDR ( the boot loader for all releases of Microsoft 's Windows NT - derived operating systems up to and including Windows XP and Windows Server 2003 )

facts.fact: In Windows Vista, Windows Server 2008 and newer versions, NTLDR was replaced.
facts.supporting_span: In Windows Vista , Windows Server 2008 and newer versions , NTLDR was replaced ;

facts.fact: In Windows Vista, Windows Server 2008 and newer versions, the boot-loader functionality is instead provided by two new components: WINLOAD.EXE and the Windows Boot Manager.
facts.supporting_span: In Windows Vista , Windows Server 2008 and newer versions , NTLDR was replaced ; the boot - loader functionality is instead provided by two new components : WINLOAD.EXE and the Windows Boot Manager .

facts.fact: In file systems such as FAT12, FAT16, FAT32, HPFS and NTFS, the VBR also contains a BIOS Parameter Block ( BPB ) that specifies the location and layout of the principal on-disk data structures for the file system.
facts.supporting_span: In file systems such as FAT12 ( except for in DOS 1.x ) , FAT16 , FAT32 , HPFS and NTFS , the VBR also contains a BIOS Parameter Block ( BPB ) that specifies the location and layout of the principal on - disk data structures for the file system .
